title: Hydrocarbons & Organic Functional Groups Comprehensive Test
syllabus: Alkanes (Wurtz reaction, Corey-House, Kolbe's electrolytic method, free radical halogenation, conformations of ethane); Alkenes & Alkynes (Markovnikov & anti-Markovnikov additions, ozonolysis, hydroboration-oxidation, oxymercuration-demercuration, Birch reduction, acidity of terminal alkynes, hydration with Hg2+/H2SO4); Haloalkanes & Haloarenes (SN1 vs SN2 kinetics and stereochemistry, E1/E2 elimination, Saytzeff vs Hofmann, Dow's process, Fittig and Wurtz-Fittig reactions); Alcohols, Phenols & Ethers (Lucas test, Victor Meyer, dehydration, Kolbe's reaction, Reimer-Tiemann, cumene process, acidity of phenols, Williamson ether synthesis, cleavage of ethers with HI); Aldehydes & Ketones (Nucleophilic addition, cyanohydrins, hemiacetals, Clemmensen & Wolff-Kishner reductions, Aldol condensation, Cannizzaro reaction, Haloform/Iodoform test, Tollens' & Fehling's tests); Carboxylic Acids (Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction, decarboxylation, esterification, relative acidic strengths); Amines & Diazonium Salts (Hofmann bromamide degradation, Gabriel phthalimide synthesis, carbylamine test, Hinsberg's reagent, azo dye coupling reactions).

questions.question: [NEET 2023] An organic compound $A$ (molecular formula $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{16}$) on reductive ozonolysis with $\text{O}_3/\text{Zn}-\text{H}_2\text{O}$ yields a single product $B$ (molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$). Compound $B$ gives a positive 2,4-DNP test and a positive iodoform test, but does NOT reduce Tollens' reagent. The structure of compound $A$ is:
questions.solution:
1. Reductive ozonolysis of alkene $A$ gives a single product $B$ ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$), meaning $A$ must be a symmetrical alkene containing 8 carbons.
2. Compound $B$ gives a positive 2,4-DNP test, indicating it is a carbonyl compound (aldehyde or ketone).
3. Compound $B$ fails Tollens' test, which means it is a ketone (not an aldehyde).
4. Compound $B$ gives a positive iodoform test, meaning it contains a methyl ketone group ($-\text{COCH}_3$).
5. The only 4-carbon ketone is butan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$).
6. Joining two molecules of butan-2-one at the carbonyl carbons by removing oxygen gives the alkene:
   $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
   This is **3,4-dimethylhex-3-ene**.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] When prop-1-yne is treated with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in the presence of $\text{HgSO}_4$ at $333\text{ K}$, the major organic product formed is:
questions.solution:
1. Hydration of an alkyne with dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{HgSO}_4$ (Kucherov's reaction) follows Markovnikov's rule.
2. Water adds across the triple bond of prop-1-yne ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$):
   $$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{Hg}^{2+}/\text{H}^+} [\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{OH})=\text{CH}_2]$$
3. The resulting enol, prop-1-en-2-ol, is unstable and undergoes rapid tautomerization into the more stable keto form:
   $$[\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{OH})=\text{CH}_2] \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3 \quad (\text{Propan-2-one})$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] In the preparation of ethers by Williamson synthesis, which set of reactants will give tert-butyl methyl ether ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{CH}_3$) as the major product?
questions.solution:
1. Williamson ether synthesis involves an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ attack of an alkoxide ion on an alkyl halide:
   $$\text{R}-\text{O}^- + \text{R}'-\text{X} \rightarrow \text{R}-\text{O}-\text{R}' + \text{X}^-$$
2. Because $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ is sensitive to steric hindrance, the alkyl halide must be unhindered (primary or methyl).
3. If a tertiary halide like $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{Br}$ is used with methoxide (Option B), the strongly basic methoxide causes E2 elimination instead of substitution, yielding 2-methylpropene as the major product.
4. Therefore, sodium tert-butoxide must be reacted with methyl bromide:
   $$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{O}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{CH}_3\text{Br} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaBr}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following compounds will undergo CANNIZZARO REACTION when treated with $50\%$ aqueous $\text{KOH}$?
questions.solution:
1. The Cannizzaro reaction is a disproportionation (redox) reaction undergone exclusively by aldehydes that **lack $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms** when heated with concentrated alkali.
2. Examine the $\alpha$-hydrogens in the options:
   - **2,2-Dimethylpropanal ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CHO}$):** The $\alpha$-carbon is quaternary and has **zero $\alpha$-hydrogens**, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction to yield neopentyl alcohol and sodium neopentanoate.
   - Acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$): $3\ \alpha$-hydrogens $\implies$ undergoes aldol condensation.
   - Propanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$): $2\ \alpha$-hydrogens $\implies$ aldol condensation.
   - 2-Methylpropanal ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCHO}$): $1\ \alpha$-hydrogen $\implies$ aldol condensation.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] An organic compound $X$ reacts with benzene sulfonyl chloride (Hinsberg's reagent) to give a clear solution which, upon acidification with dilute $\text{HCl}$, yields an insoluble solid precipitate. Compound $X$ is a:
questions.solution:
1. Reaction with Hinsberg's reagent ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{Cl}$):
   - A **primary amine ($\text{R}-\text{NH}_2$)** reacts to form an N-alkylbenzenesulfonamide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{NHR}$).
   - This product retains an acidic hydrogen attached to nitrogen directly adjacent to the strongly electron-withdrawing sulfonyl group.
   - Hence, it dissolves completely in aqueous alkali ($\text{KOH}$) to form a water-soluble potassium salt (clear solution).
   - Upon re-acidification with dilute $\text{HCl}$, the sulfonamide is regenerated and precipitates out as an insoluble solid.
2. A secondary amine forms an N,N-dialkylbenzenesulfonamide that lacks an acidic hydrogen, so it is insoluble in alkali from the start.
3. A tertiary amine does not react with Hinsberg's reagent.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] In the reaction of cumene with atmospheric oxygen followed by treatment with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, the products formed are:
questions.solution:
1. The cumene process is the predominant industrial route for the manufacture of phenol:
   - **Step 1:** Oxidation of isopropylbenzene (cumene) by bubbling air/$\text{O}_2$ produces cumene hydroperoxide via a free radical mechanism:
     $$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{OOH}$$
   - **Step 2:** Acid-catalyzed cleavage with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ triggers phenyl group migration from carbon to oxygen, yielding **phenol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH}$)** and **acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$)** as a valuable co-product.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] Which of the following compounds gives a positive CARBYLAMINE TEST (produces an extremely foul-smelling isocyanide)?
questions.solution:
1. The **carbylamine test (isocyanide test)** is an exclusive test for **primary ($1^\circ$) aliphatic and aromatic amines**.
2. When heated with chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) and alcoholic $\text{KOH}$, primary amines undergo electrophilic attack by dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$) to yield offensive-smelling carbylamines (isocyanides):
   $$\text{R}-\text{NH}_2 + \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{KOH} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{R}-\text{NC} + 3\text{KCl} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
3. **Aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$)** is a primary aromatic amine and gives phenyl isocyanide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NC}$).
4. Secondary and tertiary amines, as well as amides, do not give this reaction.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] An organic halide $X$ on heating with sodium metal in dry ether gives 2,3-dimethylbutane. Compound $X$ is:
questions.solution:
1. This reaction is the **Wurtz reaction**, which joins two alkyl radicals derived from alkyl halides:
   $$2\text{R}-\text{X} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{R}-\text{R} + 2\text{NaX}$$
2. The product is 2,3-dimethylbutane: $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$.
3. Symmetrically cleaving the central $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond shows that the reacting alkyl group $\text{R}$ is the isopropyl group, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-$.
4. Therefore, the starting alkyl halide is **2-chloropropane (isopropyl chloride)**.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] The correct order of reactivity towards nucleophilic addition reaction for the carbonyl compounds $\text{HCHO}, \text{CH}_3\text{CHO}, \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3,$ and $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$ is:
questions.solution:
1. Nucleophilic addition to a carbonyl group depends on:
   - **Electronic factors:** Electron-donating alkyl groups (+I effect) disperse positive charge on the carbonyl carbon ($\delta+$), reducing electrophilicity. Resonance (+M) from aromatic rings also decreases carbonyl electrophilicity.
   - **Steric factors:** Bulkier groups crowd the carbonyl carbon, hindering nucleophilic attack.
2. Formaldehyde ($\text{HCHO}$) has no alkyl groups $\implies$ most reactive.
3. Acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) has one +I methyl group $\implies$ less reactive than $\text{HCHO}$.
4. Acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) has two methyl groups causing +I and steric hindrance $\implies$ less reactive than aldehydes.
5. Acetophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$) has a bulky phenyl group whose $\pi$-electrons delocalize into the carbonyl group via resonance, making it the least reactive.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] When phenol is treated with chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) in the presence of aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ followed by acid hydrolysis, salicylaldehyde is obtained. The reactive intermediate involved in this Reimer-Tiemann reaction is:
questions.solution:
1. In the **Reimer-Tiemann reaction**, base-induced $\alpha$-elimination of $\text{HCl}$ from chloroform generates a neutral, electron-deficient singlet carbene:
   $$\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{OH}^- \rightleftharpoons :\!\text{CCl}_3^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \mathbf{:\!\text{CCl}_2} + \text{Cl}^-$$
2. The electrophilic **dichlorocarbene ($\mathbf{:\!\text{CCl}_2}$)** attacks the electron-rich phenoxide ring predominantly at the ortho position.
3. Subsequent hydrolysis of the intermediate dichloromethyl group yields salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde).

questions.question: [NEET 2021] The Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction involves the treatment of a carboxylic acid with $\text{Cl}_2$ or $\text{Br}_2$ in the presence of red phosphorus. The essential structural feature required in the carboxylic acid is:
options: Presence of at least one $\alpha$-hydrogen atom
Aromatic ring directly bonded to the carboxyl carbon
questions.solution:
1. In the **HVZ reaction**, red phosphorus reacts with halogen to generate $\text{PX}_3$ in situ, which converts the carboxylic acid into an acyl halide.
2. The acyl halide enolizes into an enol form that attacks molecular halogen at the $\alpha$-position, introducing halogen selectively onto the $\alpha$-carbon:
   $$\text{R}-\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{X}_2/\text{Red P}} \text{R}-\text{CH(X)}-\text{COOH}$$
3. Because enolization occurs across the $\alpha-\text{C}$ and carbonyl carbon, the carboxylic acid **must have at least one $\alpha$-hydrogen atom**.
4. Acids without $\alpha$-hydrogens (such as trimethylacetic acid or benzoic acid) fail to undergo the HVZ reaction.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Cleavage of anisole (methoxybenzene, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{O}-\text{CH}_3$) with concentrated hydroiodic acid ($\text{HI}$) at $373\text{ K}$ yields:
questions.solution:
1. Protonation of anisole gives an oxonium ion: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\overset{+}{\text{O}}(\text{H})-\text{CH}_3$.
2. The $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{O}$ bond has partial double-bond character due to resonance with the benzene ring and is exceptionally strong.
3. In contrast, the $\text{O}-\text{CH}_3$ bond is a simple $sp^3$ single bond.
4. The iodide ion ($\text{I}^-$) acts as a nucleophile and attacks the less hindered methyl carbon via an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism, displacing phenol as the leaving group:
   $$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\overset{+}{\text{O}}(\text{H})-\text{CH}_3 + \text{I}^- \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{CH}_3\text{I}$$
5. Hence, the products are **Phenol and Methyl iodide**.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] Which of the following conformations of ethane has the MAXIMUM torsional strain and potential energy?
questions.solution:
1. In the **eclipsed conformation** of ethane, the $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bonds on adjacent carbons align directly behind one another (dihedral angle $\theta = 0^\circ$).
2. The electron clouds of the adjacent $\text{C}-\text{H}$ $\sigma$-bonds experience maximum electrostatic repulsion, known as **torsional strain** (energy barrier $\approx 12.5\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$).
3. Consequently, the eclipsed conformation has the **highest potential energy and least stability**.
4. In the staggered conformation (dihedral angle $\theta = 60^\circ$), the bonds are as far apart as possible, minimizing torsional strain and providing maximum stability.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] In the Gattermann-Koch reaction, benzene is converted to benzaldehyde by treating it with:
options: $\text{CO} + \text{HCl}$ in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ and $\text{CuCl}$
questions.solution:
1. In the **Gattermann-Koch reaction**, an electrophilic formylating agent is generated in situ by reacting carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) with hydrogen chloride ($\text{HCl}$) gas in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride ($\text{AlCl}_3$) and copper(I) chloride ($\text{CuCl}$):
   $$\text{CO} + \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{AlCl}_3/\text{CuCl}} [\text{H}-\text{C}=\text{O}]^+ \text{AlCl}_4^-$$
2. The formyl cation attacks the benzene ring via electrophilic aromatic substitution, followed by proton loss to yield **benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$)**.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] A primary alcohol, a secondary alcohol, and a tertiary alcohol can be distinguished experimentally using the Lucas reagent (conc. $\text{HCl} + \text{anhydrous } \text{ZnCl}_2$). The observation for a TERTIARY alcohol is:
options: Turbidity appears immediately at room temperature
Turbidity appears within $5$ minutes on gentle heating
No turbidity appears even after heating
questions.solution:
1. The **Lucas test** proceeds through an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ pathway where the rate-determining step is carbocation formation:
   $$\text{R}-\text{OH} + \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{ZnCl}_2} \text{R}-\text{Cl} \downarrow\text{ (insoluble oily turbidity)} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
2. The rate of reaction depends on carbocation stability ($3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$):
   - **Tertiary ($3^\circ$) alcohol:** forms a very stable $3^\circ$ carbocation, producing **turbidity immediately** at room temperature.
   - **Secondary ($2^\circ$) alcohol:** produces turbidity within **$5$ minutes**.
   - **Primary ($1^\circ$) alcohol:** does not produce turbidity at room temperature; requires vigorous heating.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is exclusively used for the preparation of which class of amines?
questions.solution:
1. In Gabriel phthalimide synthesis, phthalimide is deprotonated by $\text{KOH}$ to form potassium phthalimide, which then acts as a nucleophile in an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ attack on an alkyl halide:
   $$\text{Potassium phthalimide} + \text{R}-\text{X} \rightarrow \text{N-alkylphthalimide} \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH}(aq)} \text{R}-\text{NH}_2 + \text{Sodium phthalate}$$
2. Because the reaction requires an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ displacement on $\text{R}-\text{X}$, it works cleanly only for primary alkyl halides to yield **pure primary aliphatic amines** without polyalkylation.
3. Aromatic primary amines (like aniline) **cannot be prepared** by this method because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion due to partial double-bond character.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] Benzene diazonium chloride reacts with phenol in a weakly alkaline medium ($	ext{pH} = 9-10$) to form an azo dye. The structure and color of the dye are:
questions.solution:
1. In an azo coupling reaction, the electrophilic benzene diazonium cation ($[\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2]^+$) attacks the activated phenoxide ion at the unhindered para position:
   $$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{OH}^-, \text{pH } 9-10} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{N}=\text{N}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{OH}(p) + \text{HCl}$$
2. The extended conjugated $\pi$-system absorbs blue light, giving **p-hydroxyazobenzene**, an **orange dye**.
3. (Coupling with aniline in weakly acidic medium, $\text{pH } 4-5$, gives p-aminoazobenzene, a *yellow dye*).

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Which of the following compounds gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$) when warmed with $\text{I}_2$ and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$?
questions.solution:
1. The **iodoform test** is positive for compounds containing either:
   - A methyl carbonyl group: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(=\text{O})-$
   - A methyl carbinol group that oxidizes to methyl carbonyl: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-$
2. **Pentan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$)** is a methyl ketone and undergoes base-catalyzed halogenation followed by cleavage to precipitate yellow crystals of iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$) and sodium butanoate.
3. Pentan-3-one has two ethyl groups ($-\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$), benzophenone has two phenyl groups, and 3-methylbutan-1-ol is a primary alcohol, so none give iodoform.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] In the hydroboration-oxidation of propene with diborane ($\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$) followed by alkaline $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, the final product is:
questions.solution:
1. **Hydroboration-oxidation** accomplishes the net addition of water across an alkene with **anti-Markovnikov regioselectivity** and **syn-stereospecificity**:
   $$6\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{B}_2\text{H}_6 \rightarrow 2(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2)_3\text{B}$$
2. Subsequent oxidation with alkaline hydrogen peroxide ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2/\text{OH}^-$) cleaves the $\text{B}-\text{C}$ bonds with retention of configuration:
   $$(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2)_3\text{B} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + 3\text{NaOH} \rightarrow 3\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{Na}_3\text{BO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
3. The product is **propan-1-ol** (anti-Markovnikov product).

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Hofmann bromamide degradation of propanamide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$) with $\text{Br}_2$ and $\text{KOH}$ yields:
questions.solution:
1. In the **Hofmann bromamide degradation**, an unsubstituted primary amide is treated with bromine and aqueous/alcoholic alkali to yield a primary amine containing **one carbon atom less** than the starting amide:
   $$\text{R}-\text{CONH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 + 4\text{KOH} \rightarrow \text{R}-\text{NH}_2 + \text{K}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{KBr} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
2. For propanamide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$, a 3-carbon amide):
   $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{KOH}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 \quad (\text{Ethanamine, a 2-carbon amine})$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] The reaction of an aldehyde or ketone with zinc amalgam ($\text{Zn}-\text{Hg}$) and concentrated $\text{HCl}$ to form a hydrocarbon is called:
questions.solution:
1. **Clemmensen reduction** converts the carbonyl group ($>\text{C}=\text{O}$) of aldehydes and ketones into a methylene group ($-\text{CH}_2-$) using **amalgamated zinc and concentrated hydrochloric acid**:
   $$>\text{C}=\text{O} + 4[\text{H}] \xrightarrow{\text{Zn}-\text{Hg}/\text{conc. } \text{HCl}} -\text{CH}_2- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
2. (Wolff-Kishner reduction uses $\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2/\text{KOH}$ in ethylene glycol; Rosenmund reduction uses $\text{H}_2/\text{Pd}-\text{BaSO}_4$ for acyl chlorides).

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Which of the following compounds has the HIGHEST boiling point due to extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding?
questions.solution:
1. Comparing compounds of comparable molecular weights ($\approx 72-74\text{ g mol}^{-1}$):
   - **Butan-1-ol ($	ext{M} = 74$):** Contains a polar $-\text{OH}$ group that forms extensive intermolecular **hydrogen bonds**, requiring large thermal energy to disrupt (boiling point $= 117.7^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Butanal ($	ext{M} = 72$): Polar carbonyl group with dipole-dipole interactions, but no $\text{O}-\text{H}$ bonds (boiling point $= 75.5^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Diethyl ether ($	ext{M} = 74$): Weak dipole-dipole forces (boiling point $= 34.6^\circ\text{C}$).
   - n-Butane ($	ext{M} = 58$): Non-polar, held only by weak London dispersion forces (boiling point $= -0.5^\circ\text{C}$).
2. Therefore, butan-1-ol has the highest boiling point.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] When propene is treated with chlorine gas at high temperature ($773\text{ K}$), the major product formed is:
questions.solution:
1. At room temperature in non-polar solvents, chlorine adds across the double bond of propene via an electrophilic pathway to form 1,2-dichloropropane.
2. At **elevated temperatures ($773\text{ K}$)**, homolytic cleavage of $\text{Cl}_2$ occurs to generate chlorine free radicals ($\text{Cl}^\bullet$).
3. The chlorine radical abstracts a hydrogen atom from the $sp^3$-hybridized methyl group to form the resonance-stabilized **allyl radical ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$)** rather than adding to the double bond.
4. Subsequent reaction with $\text{Cl}_2$ produces **allyl chloride (3-chloroprop-1-ene)** via allylic substitution.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following compounds is MOST REACTIVE towards electrophilic aromatic substitution?
questions.solution:
1. The rate of electrophilic aromatic substitution depends on the electron density of the benzene ring.
2. In **phenol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH}$)**, the unshared lone pair on the oxygen atom strongly donates electron density into the ring through resonance (**$+M$ effect**), strongly activating the ortho and para positions toward electrophiles.
3. Chlorobenzene has an electron-withdrawing $-I$ effect that deactivates the ring.
4. Nitrobenzene has a strongly electron-withdrawing $-\text{NO}_2$ group ($-I, -M$) that severely deactivates the ring.
5. Therefore, phenol is by far the most reactive.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] When calcium carbide ($\text{CaC}_2$) is treated with water, the hydrocarbon produced is:
questions.solution:
1. Calcium carbide contains the dicarbide (acetylide) anion: $[:\text{C}\equiv\text{C}:]^{2-}$.
2. Hydrolysis of $\text{CaC}_2$ protonates the acetylide anion, liberating **ethyne (acetylene)**:
   $$\text{CaC}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{HC}\equiv\text{CH} \uparrow$$
3. (In contrast, aluminium carbide $\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3$ contains isolated $\text{C}^{4-}$ methanide anions and hydrolyzes to methane, $\text{CH}_4$).

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Kolbe's electrolytic decarboxylation of an aqueous solution of sodium acetate yields:
options: Ethane at anode and hydrogen gas at cathode
Methane at anode and oxygen gas at cathode
Ethane at cathode and carbon dioxide at anode
Ethene at anode and hydrogen gas at cathode
questions.solution:
In Kolbe's electrolytic synthesis:
1. **At the Anode (Oxidation):**
   - Acetate ion loses an electron to form an acetate free radical:
     $$\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^\bullet + e^-$$
   - The unstable radical decarboxylates to yield carbon dioxide and a methyl radical:
     $$\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^\bullet \rightarrow \dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3 + \text{CO}_2 \uparrow$$
   - Two methyl radicals couple to form **ethane gas**:
     $$\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3 + \dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_3 \uparrow$$
2. **At the Cathode (Reduction):**
   $$2\text{H}_2\text{O} + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2 \uparrow + 2\text{OH}^-$$
Therefore, ethane and $\text{CO}_2$ evolve at the anode, while $\text{H}_2$ evolves at the cathode.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] Which of the following carboxylic acids has the HIGHEST $\text{p}K_a$ value (is the WEAKEST acid)?
questions.solution:
1. Acidity is inversely related to $\text{p}K_a$ (higher $\text{p}K_a \implies$ weaker acid).
2. Electron-donating groups (+I effect) destabilize the conjugate carboxylate anion ($\text{RCOO}^-$) by intensifying negative charge, decreasing acidity and increasing $\text{p}K_a$.
3. The tert-butyl group in **pivalic acid ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{COOH}$)** exerts the strongest +I effect and steric hindrance among the options, making it the weakest acid with the **highest $\text{p}K_a$ ($\approx 5.03$)**.
4. (Formic acid has $\text{p}K_a = 3.75$; chloroacetic acid has $\text{p}K_a = 2.87$).

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Reduction of but-2-yne with sodium in liquid ammonia (Birch reduction) produces:
questions.solution:
1. Reduction of non-terminal alkynes using **sodium in liquid ammonia ($\text{Na} / \text{liq. } \text{NH}_3$)** proceeds via a dissolving metal electron-transfer mechanism.
2. Radical anion intermediates adopt the more stable, anti-coplanar geometry to minimize steric and electrostatic repulsions between alkyl groups.
3. Protonation of the trans-radical anion yields **trans-alkenes with high stereospecificity** (anti-addition).
4. Therefore, reduction of but-2-yne yields **trans-but-2-ene**.
5. (Catalytic hydrogenation over Lindlar's catalyst, $\text{H}_2/\text{Pd}-\text{CaCO}_3$, gives *cis*-but-2-ene via syn-addition).

questions.question: [NEET 2020] Aniline on reaction with nitrous acid ($\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl}$) at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$ gives compound $A$. When $A$ is treated with cuprous chloride ($\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2$) and $\text{HCl}$, compound $B$ is formed. This reaction sequence is known as:
questions.solution:
1. Diazotization of primary aromatic amines at low temperature ($273-278\text{ K}$):
   $$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 + \text{NaNO}_2 + 2\text{HCl} \xrightarrow{0-5^\circ\text{C}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-\text{ (Compound } A) + \text{NaCl} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
2. Treatment of the diazonium salt with cuprous chloride ($\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2$) in $\text{HCl}$ replaces the diazonium group with chlorine:
   $$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- \xrightarrow{\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2/\text{HCl}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl}\text{ (Chlorobenzene, Compound } B) + \text{N}_2 \uparrow$$
3. This substitution catalyzed by cuprous halides is the **Sandmeyer reaction**.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Chlorobenzene is exceptionally INERT towards nucleophilic substitution reactions compared to chloroalkanes. Which of the following factors does NOT contribute to this low reactivity?
options: The leaving chloride group is a strong base
Resonance delocalization gives the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond partial double-bond character
The carbon attached to chlorine is $sp^2$-hybridized and holds electrons more tightly than an $sp^3$ carbon
Repulsion between the $\pi$-electron cloud of the benzene ring and the incoming nucleophile
questions.solution:
Reasons for the low reactivity of chlorobenzene toward nucleophilic substitution:
1. **Resonance effect:** Lone pairs on chlorine delocalize into the aromatic ring, giving the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond partial double-bond character ($169\text{ pm}$ vs $178\text{ pm}$ in alkyl chloride), making it difficult to break.
2. **Hybridization:** Chlorine is bonded to an $sp^2$ carbon with higher $s$-character ($33.3\%$) that holds the bond pair more tightly.
3. **Repulsion:** The electron-rich $\pi$-cloud repels approaching nucleophiles.
4. **Instability of phenyl cation:** $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ is impossible because the phenyl cation is unstable.
Chloride ion is the conjugate base of a strong acid ($\text{HCl}$) and is a **good, weak-base leaving group**, NOT a strong base. Statement A is false.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] When ethanoic acid is treated with phosphorus pentachloride ($\text{PCl}_5$), the product formed is:
questions.solution:
1. Carboxylic acids react with $\text{PCl}_5$ by nucleophilic substitution of the hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$) by chlorine to form acyl chlorides:
   $$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{PCl}_5 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCl} + \text{POCl}_3 + \text{HCl} \uparrow$$
2. The product is **ethanoyl chloride (acetyl chloride, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$)**.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following compounds gives a positive test with Tollens' reagent (silver mirror test)?
questions.solution:
1. Tollens' reagent ($[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+$) oxidizes aldehydes to carboxylates while precipitating metallic silver.
2. Most carboxylic acids do not reduce Tollens' reagent.
3. However, **formic acid ($\text{H}-\text{COOH}$)** contains both an aldehyde-like hydrogen group attached directly to the carbonyl group ($-\text{CHO}$) and a carboxyl group:
   $$\text{HCOOH} + 2[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+ + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow 2\text{Ag} \downarrow\text{ (silver mirror)} + \text{CO}_2 + 4\text{NH}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
4. Therefore, formic acid reduces Tollens' reagent to give a silver mirror.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] In the Dow's process, chlorobenzene is converted to phenol by heating with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ under drastic conditions. The reaction proceeds through which intermediate?
questions.solution:
1. Chlorobenzene reacts with sodium hydroxide under forcing conditions ($623\text{ K}$ and $300\text{ atm}$ pressure):
   $$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + 2\text{NaOH} \xrightarrow{623\text{ K}, 300\text{ atm}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
2. The elimination-addition mechanism involves elimination of $\text{HCl}$ to form an unstable, highly reactive neutral intermediate containing a formal triple bond in the aromatic ring: **Benzyne ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_4$)**.
3. Rapid nucleophilic addition of hydroxide to benzyne yields sodium phenoxide, which upon acidification gives phenol.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] What is the major product formed when phenol is treated with excess bromine water?
questions.solution:
1. In aqueous solution (a polar protic medium), phenol ionizes to form the phenoxide ion ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O}^-$).
2. The phenoxide oxygen has full negative charge and donates electron density into the ring through resonance much more strongly than a neutral $-\text{OH}$ group, activating all ortho and para positions.
3. Electrophilic bromination occurs simultaneously at both ortho positions and the para position, yielding **2,4,6-tribromophenol as a white precipitate**:
   $$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + 3\text{Br}_2(aq) \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_2\text{Br}_3\text{OH} \downarrow + 3\text{HBr}$$
4. (In non-polar solvents like $\text{CS}_2$ or $\text{CHCl}_3$, ionization is suppressed, yielding p-bromophenol as the major product).

questions.question: [NEET 2021] Which of the following alkynes will precipitate red copper(I) acetylide when treated with ammoniacal cuprous chloride?
questions.solution:
1. Terminal alkynes contain an acidic hydrogen bonded to an $sp$-hybridized triply bonded carbon ($\text{R}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{H}$).
2. When treated with ammoniacal cuprous chloride ($[\text{Cu}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+$), terminal alkynes form insoluble reddish-brown cuprous acetylide precipitates:
   $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}\equiv\text{CH} + [\text{Cu}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{Cu} \downarrow\text{ (red)} + \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{NH}_3$$
3. **But-1-yne** is a terminal alkyne and gives a positive test.
4. But-2-yne, pent-2-yne, and hex-3-yne are non-terminal (internal) alkynes with no terminal acidic hydrogen and do not react.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] An alkyl halide $A$ reacts with sodium nitrite ($\text{NaNO}_2$) in DMF to form compound $B$ as the major product. When $A$ is treated with silver nitrite ($\text{AgNO}_2$) in ethanol, compound $C$ is formed as the major product. Compounds $B$ and $C$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
1. The nitrite ion is an ambident nucleophile with two donor atoms: oxygen and nitrogen.
2. **$\text{NaNO}_2$ is predominantly ionic:** $[\text{Na}]^+ [:O-\text{N}=\text{O}]^-$. The negative charge resides on the more electronegative oxygen atom, which acts as the nucleophile to yield an **alkyl nitrite ($\text{R}-\text{ONO}$)** as the major product.
3. **$\text{AgNO}_2$ is predominantly covalent:** The silver-oxygen bond is covalent, so the oxygen lone pair is less available. The unshared lone pair on the less electronegative nitrogen atom attacks the alkyl halide, yielding a **nitroalkane ($\text{R}-\text{NO}_2$)** as the major product.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] An organic compound on treatment with pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) in dichloromethane oxidizes to an aldehyde without further oxidation to a carboxylic acid. The starting organic compound is a:
questions.solution:
1. Aqueous oxidizing agents like acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ or $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ oxidize primary alcohols past the aldehyde stage all the way to carboxylic acids.
2. **Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC, Corey's reagent)** in anhydrous $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ is a mild, selective oxidant that stops oxidation cleanly at the **aldehyde stage**:
   $$\text{R}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{PCC / } \text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2} \text{R}-\text{CHO}$$
3. Therefore, the starting material is a **primary alcohol**.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] In an aldol condensation, two molecules of ethanal (acetaldehyde) react in the presence of dilute $\text{NaOH}$ followed by heating. The final dehydration product is:
questions.solution:
1. **Aldol addition:** Deprotonation of acetaldehyde forms an enolate that attacks a second molecule of acetaldehyde to form 3-hydroxybutanal (aldol):
   $$2\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. } \text{NaOH}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$$
2. **Condensation (dehydration):** Upon heating, the $\beta$-hydroxy aldehyde loses a molecule of water to form an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated conjugated aldehyde:
   $$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CHO} \quad (\text{But-2-enal / Crotonaldehyde})$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] When ethyl chloride is heated with alcoholic $\text{KCN}$, compound $A$ is formed. Hydrolysis of $A$ with dilute $\text{HCl}$ yields compound $B$. Compound $B$ is:
questions.solution:
1. Nucleophilic substitution of ethyl chloride with alcoholic $\text{KCN}$ introduces a nitrile group:
   $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + \text{KCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}\text{ (Propanenitrile, Compound } A) + \text{KCl}$$
2. Complete acidic hydrolysis of a nitrile converts the $-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ group into a carboxylic acid:
   $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}\text{ (Propanoic acid, Compound } B) + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Phenol reacts with carbon dioxide and sodium hydroxide under pressure ($400\text{ K}, 4-7\text{ atm}$) followed by acidification to produce salicylic acid as the major product. This reaction is known as:
questions.solution:
1. **Kolbe's reaction (Kolbe-Schmitt reaction):**
   - Treatment of phenol with $\text{NaOH}$ forms sodium phenoxide, which activates the ring toward weak electrophiles.
   - Carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) acts as the electrophile and attacks the ortho position of the phenoxide ion under pressure ($4-7\text{ atm}$) at $400\text{ K}$:
     $$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{ONa} + \text{CO}_2 \xrightarrow{400\text{ K}, 4-7\text{ atm}} 2-\text{HO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{COONa}$$
   - Subsequent acidification yields **salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid)**.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] Benzene reacts with methyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to yield toluene. This reaction is an example of:
questions.solution:
1. In **Friedel-Crafts alkylation**, an alkyl halide reacts with an aromatic ring in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst:
   $$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{AlCl}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3^+ + \text{AlCl}_4^-$$
2. The generated methyl carbocation ($\text{CH}_3^+$) attacks the benzene ring via electrophilic aromatic substitution:
   $$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{CH}_3^+ \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_3\text{ (Toluene)} + \text{H}^+$$
3. Regeneration of $\text{AlCl}_3$ completes the reaction: $\text{H}^+ + \text{AlCl}_4^- \rightarrow \text{HCl} + \text{AlCl}_3$.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Which of the following compounds gives a tertiary alcohol when treated with an excess of methyl magnesium bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$) followed by hydrolysis?
questions.solution:
1. Reaction of Grignard reagents with esters:
   - One mole of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ attacks ethyl acetate, displacing ethoxide to yield a ketone (acetone):
     $$\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{MgBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{Mg(OCH}_2\text{CH}_3)\text{Br}$$
   - A second mole of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ immediately attacks acetone to form a tertiary alkoxide:
     $$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{MgBr} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{OMgBr}$$
   - Acid hydrolysis yields **2-methylpropan-2-ol (tert-butyl alcohol, a tertiary alcohol)**.
2. (Formaldehyde gives $1^\circ$ alcohol; acetaldehyde gives $2^\circ$ alcohol).

questions.question: [NEET 2021] What is the major product obtained when propene is treated with $\text{HBr}$ in the presence of benzoyl peroxide?
questions.solution:
1. In the presence of organic peroxides, $\text{HBr}$ adds to unsymmetrical alkenes via a free radical chain mechanism (**Kharasch effect / peroxide effect**).
2. The bromine free radical ($\text{Br}^\bullet$) attacks the double bond at the less substituted terminal carbon ($C_1$) to generate the **more stable secondary free radical** at $C_2$:
   $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{Br}^\bullet \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$$
3. Abstraction of hydrogen from $\text{HBr}$ yields **1-bromopropane** (anti-Markovnikov product):
   $$\text{CH}_3\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{Br}^\bullet$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following statements about the boiling points of isomeric pentanols is correct?
options: Pentan-1-ol has a higher boiling point than 2-methylbutan-2-ol due to greater surface area and stronger van der Waals forces in the unbranched isomer
2-Methylbutan-2-ol has a higher boiling point because branching increases surface area
Branching has no effect on the boiling points of alcohols
questions.solution:
1. Both pentan-1-ol ($1^\circ$) and 2-methylbutan-2-ol ($3^\circ$) have the same molecular formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$ and undergo hydrogen bonding.
2. **Pentan-1-ol** has a linear, unbranched carbon chain with a large surface area, leading to stronger intermolecular van der Waals forces.
3. **2-Methylbutan-2-ol** is spherical and compact due to branching, which reduces its contact surface area and weakens dispersion forces. Furthermore, steric hindrance around the tertiary $-\text{OH}$ group slightly weakens hydrogen bonding.
4. Therefore, **pentan-1-ol has a significantly higher boiling point ($138^\circ\text{C}$)** than 2-methylbutan-2-ol ($102^\circ\text{C}$).

questions.question: [NEET 2020] An aromatic compound $A$ ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}$) on treatment with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ gives two compounds $B$ and $C$. Acidification of compound $C$ gives benzoic acid, while compound $B$ on oxidation with acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ also gives benzoic acid. Compound $A$ is:
questions.solution:
1. Molecular formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}$ with no $\alpha$-hydrogens corresponds to **benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$)**.
2. When treated with concentrated $\text{NaOH}$, benzaldehyde undergoes the **Cannizzaro reaction** (disproportionation):
   $$2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\text{ (Compound } B) + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa}\text{ (Compound } C)$$
3. Acidification of compound $C$ (sodium benzoate) gives benzoic acid ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$).
4. Oxidation of compound $B$ (benzyl alcohol, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) with acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ also yields benzoic acid.
5. Therefore, compound $A$ is **benzaldehyde**.
